1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for a single PDP colour swatch — a clickable rectangle filled with that colour
5	 * variation's product photo. Two parts: `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry,
6	 * background, border, focus ring); `image` is the element carrying the dynamic
7	 * background-image fill — the URL itself cannot live here, see the component's own comment on
8	 * why that one `__css` spread stays dynamic.
9	 *
10	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for the three states this recipe distinguishes, not
11	 * estimated from surrounding metadata — Unselected (node 40000307:13826), Selected
12	 * (40000307:13831), Focus (40002689:3839), all under `size=Large/Rectangle`.
13	 */
14	export const ZimmColourSwatch = {
15	  parts: ['swatch', 'image'],
16	
17	  baseStyle: ({ selected }: { selected?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',
20	      cursor: 'pointer',
21	      // Figma's Rectangle width (48px). Height (72px) has no direct token — the named scale has
22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
23	      // instead. 2:3, not the incidentally different ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the
24	      // placeholder product photo pasted into that frame instance: the Selected-state node
25	      // carries its own dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3", which is the number
26	      // to trust here.
27	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
28	      aspectRatio: '2 / 3',
29	      // Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02'] in
30	      // theme/foundation/colour.ts.
31	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)',
32	      // Selected: a bottom-only border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous, a `border-b`
33	      // utility rather than a full box border. Colour is grey[900] / border.focus, the only
34	      // alias-tier value that resolves to it (border.default and border.secondary are both
35	      // light greys and never appear anywhere in this design).
36	      ...(selected
37	        ? {
38	            borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
39	            borderBottomStyle: 'solid',
40	            borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
41	          }
42	        : {}),
43	      // Focus: Figma draws this as the Selected baseline plus a ring at slightly asymmetric
44	      // per-side offsets, same colour. Not replicated literally — there is no other precedent
45	      // anywhere in this codebase for a non-uniform ring, and the asymmetry reads as that one
46	      // frame instance's export noise rather than a deliberate design decision. Mirrors
47	      // zimmNavItem.css.ts's own focus-ring block instead: a uniform `outline` + `outlineOffset`
48	      // pair, applied independently of `selected` above — a swatch can be focused without being
49	      // selected, and selected without being focused. `--zimm-focus-ring` already composites the
50	      // same border-width/colour pair used above; `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` matches
51	      // three of Figma's four side offsets.
52	      //
53	      // `position: relative` + `zIndex: 1`, scoped to this focus-visible state only: the parent
54	      // `swatches` row (zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts) is `gap: 0`, so adjacent swatches sit
55	      // flush. `outlineOffset` is positive, so the ring paints *outside* this swatch's own
56	      // border box — and with zero gap, that outward ring overlaps the very next swatch's own
57	      // box. Both swatches are plain in-flow flex items (`position: static`, `z-index: auto`),
58	      // so painting follows tree order: the later sibling paints its opaque background on top
59	      // of the earlier swatch's ring wherever the two overlap, hiding exactly the shared
60	      // (right-hand) edge — confirmed in a real Chromium render, before this fix, via
61	      // `getBoundingClientRect`/`elementFromPoint` and a screenshot: the right edge and the
62	      // right-hand slivers of the top/bottom edges were missing for every swatch with a
63	      // right-hand sibling, while the last swatch in a row (nothing to its right) rendered a
64	      // complete rectangle. `zIndex` lifts this swatch into a later, higher paint layer so its
65	      // ring is no longer covered; `position: relative` is what makes `zIndex` apply here at
66	      // all for a *general* in-flow, non-positioned element — without it `z-index` is ignored
67	      // per spec. (A `swatch` specifically is also a direct flex item of `swatches`, and the
68	      // Flexbox spec carves out flex items as one exception where `z-index` alone establishes
69	      // a stacking context even while `position` stays `static` — confirmed empirically here
70	      // too, `z-index` alone did already fix this swatch's own outline. `position: relative` is
71	      // kept anyway: it costs nothing — no `top`/`left`/etc. offset is set, so it does not move
72	      // the box — and it keeps this rule correct even if `swatch` is ever composed inside a
73	      // non-flex parent, rather than depending on a layout detail owned by a sibling file.)
74	      // Neither property is set outside `_focusVisible`, so normal (unfocused) stacking is
75	      // completely unaffected.
76	      _focusVisible: {
77	        position: 'relative',
78	        zIndex: 1,
79	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
80	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
81	      },
82	    },
83	    image: {
84	      display: 'block',
85	      width: '100%',
86	      height: '100%',
87	      backgroundSize: 'cover',
88	      backgroundPosition: 'center',
89	      backgroundRepeat: 'no-repeat',
90	    },
91	  }),
92	};

## Verdict: PASS — for the specific scope (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` fix + `index.test.tsx` regression guard)

I did not accept the report at face value. I independently reproduced every claim in it, including redoing the mutation kill myself with a byte-level restore check (backup + md5, not `git checkout`/`stash`, since that would have reverted to the pre-fix HEAD).

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | **PASS** (see reasoning on why not UNVERIFIED, below) | Recipe's `position`/`zIndex` values are byte-identical to what the original round verified against a real Chromium render (`getBoundingClientRect`/`elementFromPoint` + screenshot). This round changed zero CSS — confirmed via `git diff HEAD` on the recipe file (26 insertions, all from the prior round's fix + comment, nothing new). |
| **Pass criteria** | **PASS** | The one REWORK criterion — a validated, working test proving `position`/`zIndex` — is met and independently reproduced: real mutation kill, exact match to reported failure text. |
| **Correctness** | **PASS** | `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Full suite: 28 files / 432 tests green, including `recipeGuards.test.ts` 6/6. `eslint` clean on both files. |
| **Conformance** | **PASS** | Recipe stays namespaced (`ZimmColourSwatch`), no bare token keys, no new raw hex/px/rem introduced (`zIndex: 1` falls under the documented 0/1/-1 magic-number exception). `audit:tokens` shows zero findings for this atom's files. |
| **Completeness** | **PASS** | `index.stories.tsx` already exists and is untouched; test file now covers the regression; AC satisfied with evidence, not assertion. |
| **Restraint** | **PASS** | Test-file diff is 27 lines added, 0 removed, no new imports — one test inserted mid-`describe` block. `git status` shows exactly 4 entries; the two out-of-scope ones (`theme/components/index.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/`) were independently confirmed unrelated (registers a different, separate molecule recipe). |

### What I tried to falsify

1. **Ran the mutation myself, independently of the report.** Backed up the recipe file (md5 `53095de6...`), commented out `position: 'relative'` and `zIndex: 1`, reran the test file. Result: `8 passed | 1 failed`, `AssertionError: expected 'static' to be 'relative'` — an exact match to the reported failure. Restored from backup, confirmed **byte-identical** via `diff` and matching md5, reran: `9/9 passing` again. This proves the test is load-bearing, not decorative — it fails on exactly the regression it claims to guard and does not fail spuriously.
2. **Checked the test diff isn't hiding a change to the 8 pre-existing tests or a new import that could mask a different result.** `git diff` shows purely additive: one new `test()` block, 0 deletions, uses only imports already present (`render`, `ChakraProvider`, `MemoryRouter`, `ZimmTokensGlobal`, `ZimmColourSwatch`).
3. **Checked the selector actually targets the styled node**, not a decoy. `grep`'d `index.tsx`: `data-testid="colour-swatch"` sits on the exact element carrying `__css={styles.swatch}` — the part the recipe's `_focusVisible` block styles. (Also implicitly proven by the mutation: if the selector missed, `.focus()` on `undefined` would throw, not produce `'static'`.)
4. **Checked the "unrelated in-flight work is untouched" claim** rather than trusting it. `theme/components/index.ts`'s diff is exactly a `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` import + registration line — a different recipe, unrelated to this fix. The untracked `zimmColourSwatchGroup/` folder is a self-contained new directory with no overlap.
5. **Ran `tsc`, full `npm run test`, `eslint`, and `audit:tokens` myself** rather than trusting the reported numbers — all matched exactly (432/432, clean tsc, clean lint, zero token findings on this atom).

### What I could not verify

- **A fresh real-browser screenshot, this round.** I did not re-drive Chromium myself this round — see part (b) below for why I don't think that's required here.
- I did not re-verify jsdom's general `:focus`/`position`/`zIndex` support theoretically — I consider this moot, since the mutation kill is direct empirical proof for this exact case, which is a stronger bar than a theoretical argument would be.

No defects found. Nothing to instruct back to the implementer.

---

### (a) Commit readiness

Yes — ready for its own commit, separate from Step 3's molecule work. `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` was committed at `ab04241` *without* this fix; the current working-tree diffs on `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (the fix) and `index.test.tsx` (the regression guard) together form one coherent, self-contained unit with no dependency on the uncommitted `zimmColourSwatchGroup/` or `theme/components/index.ts` changes.

Suggested conventional-commit message:

```
fix(ui-kits): keep focus ring visible on adjacent colour swatches (SFCC-91)

_focusVisible now sets position: relative + zIndex: 1 on ZimmColourSwatch
so a focused swatch's outline ring isn't painted over by the next
zero-gap sibling's opaque background. Adds a regression test asserting
the resolved position/zIndex via getComputedStyle — mutation-verified to
fail (position: static) with the fix reverted.
```

### (b) Are the existing screenshots sufficient, or does this need a fresh human look?

**My call: the existing real-Chromium before/after evidence is sufficient — no fresh screenshot pass is required to close this out.** Reasoning:

- The actual CSS values (`position: relative`, `zIndex: 1`) have not changed by a single byte since the original investigation round produced that evidence (confirmed via `git diff HEAD` above) — there is no new visual surface to re-check.
- This round's entire change is an *additive automated test in jsdom*, which cannot itself introduce a visual regression — it only asserts against the already-verified declaration.
- Re-screenshotting an unchanged CSS value every time a regression test is added for it would be re-verifying something that hasn't moved, not something new.

The one honest caveat, which I'd surface as the **residual risk** rather than a blocker: a jsdom `getComputedStyle` assertion is a proxy for "the declaration resolves correctly," not for "the paint/compositing order is actually correct in a real browser." If a future change ever touches `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `gap` value or flex layout, this Vitest test would not by itself re-catch a real-paint overlap regression the way the original manual `elementFromPoint`-based check did. That's a good candidate for a future Storybook `play` or Playwright visual assertion (reusing the original investigation's `elementFromPoint`-at-the-shared-edge technique) — but it's a strengthening follow-up, not a gap in what this specific REWORK round was asked to close.
